title: Which grids can be filled in more than one way?
description: Two of the book's grids are compared by counting empty tiles against the four sides. The grid with four empty tiles is forced at every step, and the grid with five empty tiles allows a free choice, shown by two different fillings.
teaching_notes: One idea: each side fixes one empty tile, so a grid with more empty tiles than sides leaves a tile to choose freely. Watch for students who think more given numbers mean more ways to fill the grid.

video_script.why: The child counts empty tiles against the four sides to see which grids leave a free choice.
video_script.substitution: Two of the book's grids with a border sum, with three and four numbers given.
video_script.anchor: a square of nine tiles from the book, with the middle tile missing
video_script.payoff_line: A grid has many fillings when it has more empty tiles than its four sides can fix.

final_answer.value: Open-ended. The first grid can be filled in many ways, and the second grid in only one way, because its four empty tiles are fixed by its four sides.
final_answer.spoken: the first grid can be filled in many ways, and the second grid in only one way

hold_back: Open-ended. The first grid can be filled in many ways, and the second grid in only one way, because its four empty tiles are fixed by its four sides.
maths_rules: first grid (grid A), border sum 4, given -10 top left, -5 middle right, 9 bottom left: 5 empty tiles, 4 sides
second grid (grid B), border sum -2, given 6 top left, 8 top middle, -5 middle right, -2 bottom middle: 4 empty tiles, 4 sides
second grid forced: top right 6 + 8 = 14, move down 16, -16; bottom right -16 + (-5) = -21, move up 19, 19; bottom left -2 + 19 = 17, move down 19, -19; middle left 6 + (-19) = -13, move up 11, 11

first grid: middle left -10 + 9 = -1, move up 5, 5; top right free; with top right 4: top middle 10, bottom right 5, bottom middle -10; with top right 3: top middle 11, bottom right 6, bottom middle -11
check of the second filling of the first grid: top -10 + 11 + 3 = 4; right 3 + (-5) + 6 = 4; bottom 9 + (-11) + 6 = 4; left -10 + 5 + 9 = 4
each side fixes one empty tile; more empty tiles than sides leaves a tile to choose freely
video_script.design: Two grids side by side with the empty tiles counted. The second grid fills tile by tile with each tile forced. The first grid is filled twice, with the free tile circled.
open_questions: The worklist answer is open-ended, so the video settles the first two grids of the book's border sum set and does not claim to list every grid.

<bookmark mark='name'/>All four sides of a grid add up to one number.

<bookmark mark='rule'/>Each side gives one rule, and one rule can fix one empty tile.

narration: <bookmark mark='top'/>Step two, try the second grid.
Six plus eight is fourteen, so move down sixteen. The top right tile is negative sixteen.
<bookmark mark='right'/>Negative sixteen plus negative five is negative twenty-one, so move up nineteen. The bottom right tile is nineteen.
<bookmark mark='bottom'/>Negative two plus nineteen is seventeen, so move down nineteen. The bottom left tile is negative nineteen.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Six plus negative nineteen is negative thirteen, so move up eleven. The middle left tile is eleven.
Every tile was fixed, with no choice at all.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: grid A, border sum 4. Left column: -10 + 9 = -1, move up 5, middle left = 5. The top right tile is free. Choose 4: top middle 10, bottom right 5, bottom middle -10. Choose 3: -10 + 3 = -7, move up 11, top middle = 11; 3 + (-5) = -2, move up 6, bottom right = 6; 9 + 6 = 15, move down 11, bottom middle = -11

narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step three, try the first grid.
Negative ten plus nine is negative one, so move up five. The middle left tile is five.
<bookmark mark='free'/>The top right tile can then be chosen freely.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Choose four, and the other tiles are ten, five and negative ten.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Choose three instead.
The top middle tile is eleven, and the bottom right tile is six.
The bottom middle tile is negative eleven.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check: second filling of grid A. Top row: -10 + 11 + 3 = 4. Right column: 3 + (-5) + 6 = 4. Bottom row: 9 + (-11) + 6 = 4. Left column: -10 + 5 + 9 = 4

marks.check: the four sides of the second filling light up one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check the second filling of the first grid.
The top row, negative ten plus eleven plus three, makes four.
<bookmark mark='right'/>The right column, three plus negative five plus six, makes four.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The bottom row and the left column also make four, so the filling works.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A grid has many fillings when it has more empty tiles than its four sides can fix.
<bookmark mark='one'/>The first grid has five empty tiles, so one tile may be chosen freely.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The second grid has four empty tiles, so it has only one filling.
